official.deadline_note: Both the Master's programme application and the Tilburg University Waiver webform must be completed by 1 April 2027; applicants are informed of the outcome by 1 June 2027. This matches the general non-EEA Fall-intake programme deadline on Tilburg's admissions page. Waivers are not available for the February intake.
official.status_note: The official page states 21 waivers are available for the 2027-2028 academic year (September intake), with applications currently accepted until 1 April 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Official wording: "Value: 50% waiver of the institutional tuition fee for all regular (non-Research) one-year Master's programs" and "The Tilburg University Waiver reduces your institutional tuition fee by 50%".
benefits: 50% reduction of the institutional tuition fee for all regular (non-Research) one-year Master's programs

21 waivers for the 2027-2028 academic year, divided by Schools: 6 Tilburg School of Economics and Management, 6 Tilburg Law School, 2 Tilburg School of Social and Behavioral Sciences, 6 Tilburg School of Humanities and Digital Sciences, 1 Tilburg School of Catholic Theology
Part of Tilburg University's Diversity, Equity & Inclusion (DEI) commitment to reduce structural barriers to postgraduate education
eligibility: Hold a non-EEA nationality and have completed, or be due to complete before the start of the Master's program, your most recent degree in one of the designated eligible countries (59-country list including Afghanistan, Brazil, China, Egypt, Ghana, India, Indonesia, Kenya, Mexico, Morocco, Nigeria, Pakistan, Peru, Philippines, Serbia, Taiwan, Turkiye, Ukraine, Vietnam and Zambia)
It must be your first Master's program at Tilburg University
Submit a complete application for a regular one-year Master's program starting in September 2027 by April 1, 2027
Complete the Tilburg University Waiver application form before April 1, 2027
Do not hold any other tuition-fee waiver; the waiver cannot be combined with any other scholarship that covers all or part of your tuition fee
Applicants for Research Master's programs are not eligible (see the Research Master Scholarship instead)
Only students directly admitted to a Master's program may apply; students who are or have been enrolled in a Pre-Master's program are not eligible
requirements: Submit a complete application for one of the regular one-year Master's programs starting in September 2027 by April 1, 2027
Complete the Tilburg University Waiver application form before the same April 1, 2027 deadline
Demonstrate English proficiency at the time of application, in line with the September 2027 intake admission requirements
Applicants who will complete their current degree before the Master's program starts must have completed that degree in an eligible country
documents: Tilburg University Waiver application webform, submitted before April 1, 2027
Complete Master's programme application via Studielink and OSIRIS Aanmeld, including proof of English proficiency at the time of application
One-time EUR 100 application fee for applicants with a non-Dutch diploma
selection_criteria: If more eligible candidates apply than waivers available, a random lottery determines the recipients
Only applicants who are conditionally or unconditionally admitted to a Master's program are included in the draw
A waiver becomes effective only after unconditional admission has been confirmed

If fewer than 21 waivers are accepted after the main selection, remaining awards are assigned by lottery to non-EEA applicants who submitted the form before April 1, 2027 and hold conditional or unconditional admission by June 1, 2027
coverage: 50% of the institutional tuition fee only; the official page states all regular non-EEA funding and immigration requirements still apply and recipients must still show funds for the remaining 50% of tuition plus IND living-cost funds
application_method: Submit the Master's programme application through Studielink and OSIRIS Aanmeld by April 1, 2027 (September intake)
Complete the Tilburg University Waiver application webform before April 1, 2027
Pay the one-time EUR 100 application fee (applicants with a non-Dutch diploma) to enable submission
official.application_route: Two-step: apply to an eligible regular one-year Master's programme in Studielink/OSIRIS Aanmeld and complete the Tilburg University Waiver webform, both before 1 April 2027.
official.citizenship_residency: Non-EEA nationality required, with the most recent degree completed (or due to be completed before the Master's starts) in one of the 59 designated countries
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the waiver is aimed specifically at international applicants with a non-EEA nationality whose most recent degree was completed in a designated country
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Regular (non-Research) one-year Master's programmes only; the stated exception is the two-year Master in Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence, including the Artificial Intelligence for Psychological Research and Artificial Intelligence en Cybersecurity tracks. Research Master's and Pre-Master's programmes are not eligible.
official.duration: One academic year of tuition for a regular Master's programme; the two-year Master in Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence is also eligible
official.description: Tilburg University describes the waiver as halving the institutional tuition fee for exceptional international master's applicants who hold a non-EEA nationality and completed their previous degree in an eligible country, with 21 awards each year supporting talented students worldwide as part of the university's Diversity, Equity & Inclusion commitment.
official.program_type: Partial tuition-fee waiver awarded by the university (DEI scheme), allocated by lottery among eligible admitted applicants
official.english_requirement: For the September 2027 intake (official admission page): IELTS Academic minimum total score 6.5 with minimum subscore 6.0 in Writing and Speaking (IELTS Online not accepted); TOEFL iBT taken on or after 21 January 2026: minimum total 5 with subscores 5 for Writing and 5 for Speaking (before that date: total 90, subscores 22 Writing / 21 Speaking); Cambridge C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency: minimum total score of 180 with subscore 180 for Writing and Speaking. Results must be from a single test date and no older than two years; exemption is possible with an English-taught degree proven by transcript, diploma supplement or an official university statement at C1 level.

not_confirmed: funding_amount, funding_currency, funding_period: the official pages publish the value only as a 50% reduction of the institutional tuition fee; the fee itself varies by programme and is set per academic year, so no absolute euro figure for the waiver is published
verification.notes: Checked the official DEI-waiver page (value, 21 waivers, eligibility, deadline 1 April 2027, lottery, non-deferrable, IND financial reminder), the Master's tuition-fee overview page, the tuition-fee rates page (institutional fee context), and the admission page (English requirements for the September 2027 intake).

applicant_utility.summary: This is a lottery-based 50% tuition reduction, not a merit award: once your programme application and the waiver webform are both submitted by 1 April 2027, the draw turns on your nationality and the country of your most recent degree rather than your grades. Only 21 waivers exist, and only applicants with conditional or unconditional admission enter the draw, so the timing and completeness of your programme application is what actually controls your chances. Budget for the remaining half of the institutional fee plus Dutch IND living-cost proof before accepting, because the award cancels if you defer or withdraw.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EEA nationals from one of the 59 designated countries who can fund the other 50% of tuition and meet IND living-cost proof, and who are applying to a regular one-year taught Master's in economics, law, social sciences, humanities or theology.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm both your non-EEA nationality and that your most recent degree was (or will be before the programme starts) completed in a country on the designated list
Submit the Master's programme application in Studielink and OSIRIS Aanmeld well before 1 April 2027, then complete the waiver webform before the same date
Hold a valid English test result at application time (the September 2027 thresholds are IELTS 6.5 with 6.0 in Writing and Speaking, or the new-scale TOEFL iBT 5)
Verify your target programme is a regular one-year taught Master's (not a Research Master's, not entered via a Pre-Master's)
Check you hold no other tuition-fee waiver or tuition-covering scholarship
common_rejection_risks: Most recent degree completed in a country that is not on the 59-country designated list, or an EEA nationality
Entering via a Pre-Master's route instead of direct admission, or having been enrolled in a Tilburg Pre-Master's
Submitting the waiver webform late while the programme application was on time (or vice versa) - both must be complete by 1 April 2027
Holding another tuition-fee waiver or a scholarship that covers part of tuition, which bars combination
Applying for the February intake, for which no waivers are offered
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The remaining ~50% of the institutional tuition fee (Tilburg's non-EU/EEA Master's institutional fee was EUR 19,900 for 2026-2027; rates are set per academic year), living costs of about EUR 1,000-1,200 per month per Tilburg's own estimate, and the Dutch IND immigration fee.
document_audit: The waiver webform and the programme application are separate submissions - finishing one does not enter you into the draw without the other
English test results must already exist and meet the thresholds when you apply; a booked-but-unfinished test will stall the application
If your degree is still in progress, the institution where you complete it must sit on the eligible-country list
alerts: The waiver is non-deferrable: deferring or withdrawing cancels the award
Recipients must still satisfy IND financial proof - funds for the remaining 50% of tuition plus living costs - before the visa process can begin
The waiver only becomes effective after unconditional admission is confirmed, so conditional admission at 1 June 2027 still leaves work to do
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply to the programme through Studielink plus OSIRIS Aanmeld, submit the waiver webform, await the lottery draw among conditionally/unconditionally admitted eligible applicants, then confirm unconditional admission to activate the waiver.

official.deadline_note: The complete Master's programme application must be submitted by 1 January 2027, 23:59 CET for scholarship consideration, while the general Master's application deadline is later (1 May 2027, 23:59 CET for all Master's programmes). TU/e confirms selections by the end of March 2027.
official.status_note: The official page states the information applies to applications for the academic year 2027-2028, with the application deadline of 1 January 2027 still ahead and approximately 35 scholarships available.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Official wording: "EUR 7,500 per academic year, for two years (if enrolled and meeting the study progress requirements)" and "The scholarships are not full scholarships and do not cover the total cost of your studies. You should be prepared to contribute significantly to your tuition and living expenses".
benefits: EUR 7,500 per academic year, for two years (if enrolled and meeting the study progress requirements)
Paid in monthly instalments to a Dutch (or SEPA) bank account
Approximately 35 scholarships: 20 for EEA students and 15 for non-EEA students
Recognition of academic merit and potential, enhancing your CV and professional profile (official wording)
eligibility: Have applied for a full-time Master's program (or an eligible track) at TU/e for the 2027-2028 academic year, starting on 1 September 2027, in Applied Physics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or Mathematics & Computer Science
Meet the specific admission requirements of the Master's program applied to
Have completed a non-Dutch high school diploma or university bachelor's degree, or both
Have not completed higher education (university or university of applied sciences) in the Netherlands; exchange programs are allowed
Have excellent academic results, as demonstrated by your latest grade transcript (GPA of at least 7.5 on a 10-point scale)
Will meet all requirements for obtaining a Dutch entry visa and residence permit
Are not applying for a joint Master's with Tilburg University (JADS) or a European Double Degree program
Have not been admitted based on an admission decision from a previous intake
requirements: Confirm in your Master's application that you would like to be considered for the scholarship
Include a brief motivation explaining why you believe you are a strong candidate
Submit your complete application by 1 January 2027, 23:59 CET
Gain at least 45 ECTS in the first year to receive the second-year scholarship, and be expected to graduate within 36 months
documents: Complete TU/e Master's programme application with all required digital documents uploaded before the deadline
Latest grade transcript demonstrating a GPA of at least 7.5/10
Official English language test score report uploaded in the online application form (no older than two years)
Brief motivation statement included within the application
selection_criteria: TU/e International Office first checks all applications for eligibility
Eligible applications are ranked by the Scholarship Selection Committee consisting of the Rector Magnificus, Dean of Education, Director Finance & Control, and Director Education & Student Affairs
Approximately 35 awards split 20 EEA / 15 non-EEA; TU/e states only about 2% of applicants will receive the scholarship

The selection outcome cannot be appealed; scholarships cannot be deferred, are non-transferable to Master's programs outside the four eligible departments, and the award amount is final and non-negotiable
coverage: EUR 7,500 per academic year for two years towards study costs, paid in monthly instalments; not a full scholarship and does not cover living costs
For non-EEA students, part of the first-year award is funded by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science through the NL Scholarship (which cannot be applied for separately)
application_method: Apply for an eligible Master's program (or track) in one of the four eligible departments through the regular TU/e admissions route (Studielink registration plus the online application in Osiris)
Confirm in the application that you wish to be considered for the scholarship and include a brief motivation
Submit the complete application by 1 January 2027, 23:59 CET
official.application_route: No separate scholarship form: consideration is automatic with the regular TU/e Master's application, provided you tick the scholarship option, add the short motivation, and submit by 1 January 2027, 23:59 CET.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to both EEA and non-EEA international students (20 EEA and 15 non-EEA awards); applicants must have completed a non-Dutch high school diploma or bachelor's degree and must not have completed higher education in the Netherlands
official.international_eligibility: Yes - designed for talented international students (EEA and non-EEA) with non-Dutch prior education; students with completed Dutch higher education (other than exchange) are excluded
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Master's programmes in Applied Physics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or Mathematics & Computer Science, including the listed MSc programmes and tracks (e.g. MSc Artificial Intelligence and Engineering Systems, MSc Computer Science and Engineering incl. Cybersecurity and Systems and AI, MSc Data Science and AI, MSc Electrical Engineering, MSc Embedded Systems, MSc Industrial and Applied Mathematics, MSc Mechanical Engineering incl. Aerospace Systems Engineering, MSc Science and Technology of Nuclear Fusion, MSc Sustainable Energy Technology, MSc Systems and Control, MSc Automotive Technology, MSc Applied Physics). JADS joint Master's with Tilburg University and European Double Degree programmes are excluded; the award is non-transferable to other departments.
official.duration: Two academic years (second-year payment requires at least 45 ECTS in the first year)
official.description: TU/e awards this Scholarship for Excellence to highly talented international students who want to shape the future of microchip technology and are applying to a Master's programme in Applied Physics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering or Mathematics & Computer Science; the scholarships are funded by the national Beethoven Program, a strategic Dutch government investment in the microchip sector.
official.program_type: University merit scholarship (partial), funded through the national Beethoven Programme
official.english_requirement: Official TU/e language proficiency page for the 2027-2028 intake: IELTS Academic minimum overall 6.5 with minimum 6.0 per section, one test date, IELTS Online and One Skill Retake not accepted; TOEFL iBT from 21 January 2026 minimum 4.5 overall and 4.5 per section (before that date: 90 overall and 21 per section); Cambridge C1 Advanced 176 or C2 Proficiency 180, minimum 169 per section; LanguageCert Academic 70 (min 65 per section); Pearson PTE Academic 61 (min 46 per section). Test results must be no older than 2 years and uploaded as an official score report in the application; exemptions apply for certain prior education.

verification.notes: Amount (EUR 7,500 per academic year for two years, monthly instalments), deadline (1 January 2027, 23:59 CET), eligibility, selection and study-progress rules confirmed on the official TU/e scholarship page; English requirements from TU/e's official language proficiency requirements page (2027-2028 intake); living-cost and fee context from TU/e's tuition fees and other study costs page.

applicant_utility.summary: Consideration is automatic with your Master's application - there is no separate scholarship form - but you must tick the scholarship option and add a short motivation before the 1 January 2027, 23:59 CET deadline, and only applicants to programmes in Applied Physics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering or Mathematics & Computer Science qualify. The award is EUR 7,500 per year for two years, paid monthly, and TU/e is explicit that it is not a full scholarship, so plan to fund most of the tuition plus at least EUR 10,000-12,000 a year of living costs yourself. With only about 2% of applicants winning, treat it as a bonus rather than the basis of your funding plan.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-GPA (7.5/10 or better) applicants to TU/e's engineering and applied-science Master's programmes who can cover the remaining costs and want a competitive partial award alongside their admission.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your target programme is one of the eligible MScs/tracks in Applied Physics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering or Mathematics & Computer Science
Complete the Studielink registration plus the Osiris application with every required document uploaded before 1 January 2027, 23:59 CET
Tick the scholarship option and write the brief motivation inside the application
Check your latest transcript shows a GPA of at least 7.5/10 at the time of application (conditional acceptance on CGPA is not possible)
Book IELTS/TOEFL early so the official score report is verifiable and uploaded in the application
common_rejection_risks: An incomplete application on 1 January 2027 - a missing upload means no scholarship consideration even if admission later succeeds
Applying to a joint Master's with Tilburg University (JADS) or a European Double Degree programme, which are excluded
Prior completed higher education in the Netherlands (exchange programmes are the only exception)
A latest-transcript GPA below 7.5/10, or admission based on a previous intake's decision
Falling short of 45 ECTS in year one, which forfeits the second-year payment
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The balance of tuition beyond EUR 7,500 per year plus at least EUR 10,000-12,000 per year in living costs per TU/e's own budget guidance (rent about EUR 400-700 per month), the EUR 100 application fee, and the guarantee fee that non-EEA admitted students pay up front.
document_audit: The motivation must live inside the same application - there is no separate scholarship dossier
The English score report must be the official document, from a single test date, under two years old, and verifiable via your TRF, appointment, verification, score report or candidate number
The grade transcript demonstrating the 7.5 GPA must be the latest one; TU/e does not grant conditional acceptance on CGPA
alerts: 1 January 2027 is the scholarship-eligibility deadline, not the general admission deadline (1 May) - applying in spring forfeits scholarship consideration even if admission is still possible
For non-EEA winners, part of the first-year award comes via the national NL Scholarship and cannot be applied for separately; proof of sufficient financial means for the IND is still required
The outcome cannot be appealed, the award cannot be deferred or transferred to other departments, and winners must sign a scholarship agreement
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply to an eligible Master's programme via Studielink and Osiris, tick the scholarship box with your motivation, submit everything by 1 January 2027, 23:59 CET; the International Office screens eligibility, the selection committee ranks, and winners sign a scholarship agreement after confirmation by end of March 2027.
